subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Alkanes are generally unreactive because they:
options: Contain only strong, nonpolar C-C and C-H single bonds
questions.explain: Saturated, nonpolar alkanes resist attack by most reagents.

questions.q: Alkanes react with halogens (e.g. chlorine) in ultraviolet light by:
questions.explain: UV light initiates a radical chain: initiation, propagation and termination.

questions.q: In free-radical substitution, the initiation step involves:
options: Homolytic breaking of the halogen bond to form radicals
questions.explain: UV light causes homolytic fission of Cl2 into two chlorine radicals.

questions.q: The reaction of methane with chlorine in UV light produces:
questions.explain: Substitution replaces an H with Cl: CH4 + Cl2 → CH3Cl + HCl.

questions.q: Alkenes typically react by:
options: Electrophilic addition across the double bond
questions.explain: The electron-rich C=C is attacked by electrophiles, adding across the double bond.

questions.q: The reaction of ethene with bromine (Br2) produces:
questions.explain: Bromine adds across the double bond; the decolourising of bromine water tests for alkenes.

questions.q: Bromine water is decolourised by an alkene but not by an alkane because:
options: Only the alkene undergoes addition with bromine
questions.explain: The C=C double bond reacts with bromine, removing its colour; saturated alkanes do not.

questions.q: The addition of hydrogen to an alkene (with a nickel catalyst) produces:
questions.explain: Hydrogenation adds H2 across the double bond, forming the saturated alkane.

questions.q: Adding steam (H2O) to ethene with an acid catalyst produces:
questions.explain: Hydration of ethene is an industrial route to ethanol.

questions.q: Halogenoalkanes react with nucleophiles such as hydroxide ions by:
questions.explain: A nucleophile replaces the halogen; e.g. OH- converts a halogenoalkane to an alcohol.

questions.q: A nucleophile is a species that:
options: Donates a lone pair of electrons to form a bond
questions.explain: Nucleophiles ('nucleus-loving') are electron-pair donors attracted to positive centres.

questions.q: Warming a halogenoalkane with aqueous sodium hydroxide produces:
questions.explain: Nucleophilic substitution by OH- replaces the halogen with a hydroxyl group.

questions.q: In the propagation steps of free-radical substitution:
options: Radicals react to form products and regenerate radicals
Two radicals combine to end the chain
questions.explain: Propagation sustains the chain by producing new radicals.

questions.q: The termination step of a radical chain reaction involves:
options: Two radicals combining to form a stable molecule
questions.explain: Termination removes radicals, ending the chain (e.g. Cl. + Cl. → Cl2).

questions.q: Oxidation of a primary alcohol (e.g. with acidified dichromate) first produces:
questions.explain: Primary alcohols oxidise to aldehydes, then to carboxylic acids on further oxidation.

questions.q: Oxidation of a secondary alcohol produces:
questions.explain: Secondary alcohols are oxidised to ketones, which resist further oxidation.

questions.q: Tertiary alcohols are resistant to oxidation because:
options: The carbon bearing -OH has no hydrogen atom to remove
questions.explain: Oxidation of an alcohol removes an H from the carbinol carbon; tertiary alcohols lack this H.

questions.q: Reacting a carboxylic acid with an alcohol (acid catalyst) produces:
questions.explain: Esterification is a condensation reaction forming an ester and releasing water.

questions.q: Complete combustion of an alkane produces:
questions.explain: Alkanes are used as fuels; complete combustion gives CO2 and H2O.

questions.q: Electrophilic addition to an alkene is favoured because the double bond:
options: Is a region of high electron density attractive to electrophiles
Contains a lone pair on carbon
questions.explain: The pi electrons attract electrophiles, initiating addition.
